correctness.rationale: Use arXiv:2307.08439 Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 3.8 to identify outer phi-derivations with weighted degree-one crown cohomology. The allowed-edge count is 2m for identity, m for adjacent rotations, zero for other nonidentity rotations, and four for every reflection. Coboundary rank is 2m-1 or 2m according to the scalar holonomy in the identity case, zero for nonidentity rotations, and two for reflections because exactly two fixed vertices yield independent disjoint-support coboundaries. The group order follows from unit size (q-1)^(2m)q^(2m), central units q-1, the (q-1)-sized quotient of multiplicative weightings by vertex potentials, and 2m poset automorphisms. The exact probability distribution and moment formulas are arithmetical consequences. Direct defining-identity checks over prime fields for m=3..5 passed 144 cases; 900 cochain cases and 51 moments also passed. The proof does not use finite testing as infinite certification.

originality.rationale: The closest primary result (Fornaroli–Khrypchenko, arXiv:2307.08439) proves an abstract cohomology reduction and gives individual crown examples: Examples 3.14–3.15 for the two-crown and Example 3.22 for one four-crown symmetry. These individual cases are prior; the assessed claim instead computes every dihedral automorphism and every multiplicative twist for all m>=3, then counts all automorphisms by dimension and derives the unusual limiting-law/mean discrepancy. A separate 2021 crown paper addresses Lie automorphism properness, not twisted derivation quotient dimensions; 2024 incidence-algebra derivation work treats ordinary derivations. Accessible claim comparisons and targeted terminology/alias searches produced no covering numerical theorem; absence of hits is not proof of global novelty. An implicit broader Hochschild-cohomology specialization remains a risk.

value.rationale: The dimension of the outer twisted derivation space is a motivated obstruction to innerness for finite incidence algebras. The theorem gives a complete sharp classification for every automorphism of an infinite natural crown family. It distinguishes reflections (dimension 2), adjacent rotations (dimension m), generic rotations (zero) and identity-holonomy resonance (zero or one). The induced distribution has rare m-dimensional events of probability 1/m, making expected dimensions converge to 2 despite weak convergence to a distribution of mean 1; this is a mathematically meaningful asymptotic surprise, not merely a finite count.
